objective: Let a viewer explore a small fictional river village at civil dusk, lit only by paper lanterns, and select any building to learn what it is and how it was built.
custom_choices: Terrain: a rolling height field carved by a river, flattened into a west-bank terrace and raised into an east bluff, with a levelled pad stamped under every building (world/terrain.js). No blueprint covers terrain.

River: a THREE.Reflector under two transparent ripple layers whose canvas normal maps scroll along 37 and 128 degrees - the look's 'every lantern appears twice' technique made real rather than faked with mirrored sprites.
Paper lanterns and their cords: lathe geometry hung between two lantern-post 'hook' sockets, swaying on seeded sines.
Lane ribbons that sample the height field, so a lane climbing to the bridge stays on the ground.
Selection ring instead of a material tint: kit materials come from a shared cache, so tinting one building would tint every clone of it.
The mill is built at T2 rather than its available T3 bake, because the bake freezes the wheel.

runtime.render_scheduling: Demand-driven RAF, max 60 fps, hidden-tab suspension, camera/selection/control invalidation; 2048px directional shadow map, one 512px point shadow.

scenes.motion: decorative (procedural gait, scrolling ripple maps, seeded sway)
entities: hero: Ferryman's cottage, T3 Blender-baked GLB
landmark: watch tower, 9.5 m on a 3.4 m bluff
stone bridge over the river, the only large curved mass
river mill with a turning overshot wheel
3 further cottages, a long hall, 3 market stalls
10 lantern posts, 7 hanging paper lanterns, 12 dynamic point lights
scale cue: 1.75 m biped figure, 2.0 m doors, 0.35 m lanterns
2 biped walkers, 2 quadruped walkers on seeded routes
boundaries: Fictional town, river and businesses; no real place, festival, date or brand is depicted.
No ecology, hydrology or structural claim: the kits are authored creative starting points.
Terrain, water depth and building spacing are composed for the frame, not surveyed.

physical_contract.scope: metres; gait phase advances by distance travelled over stride length so a planted foot holds its world position
physical_contract.time: variable dt capped at 0.05 s per frame; dt = 0 while paused
limits: No collision, no ground contact solving beyond a height-field lookup, no dynamics.

selection_scope: The style and lighting records guided the palette, fog, light values, camera and post; the blueprint records supplied every building, prop, plant and creature. Terrain, water, paper lanterns, lanes, embers and the selection UI are custom and are listed under custom_choices.
